chunks: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and cause water to descend thereby, and bring forth thereby all kinds of fruits. Thus will We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember.
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran use the imagery of rain and clouds to explain the resurrection of the dead?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the tangible signs of Allah’s mercy in nature, linking the physical resurrection of the earth to the spiritual resurrection of the soul. The metaphor of 'heavy clouds' carrying rain to 'dead land' underscores the transformative power of divine will, serving as a profound reminder for believers to reflect on the inevitability of the Hereafter.
